lines.t: A letter came for you — Larkhollow postmark, smells of varnish and kettle. Sit. I'll see to your troupe.
"{player} — Tamsin's Keynote! I'm proud of you. Now, about the name on that work order."
"Odile and I built our first Chime together."
"She always said a stone that sings whenever it likes is a stone nobody's in charge of. I thought she meant it as a joke."
"She was my apprentice once. The best I had. Mind yourself on Highscar, and keep {starter} close. —O."
Healed, rested, ready. Next!
Welcome to the Galewick Hearthrest! Rest, ledger, recall — pick one. The queue's long. It isn't. But it might be.
Healed, rested, ready. Next!
Buying? Wonderful. While you choose, did you hear about the miller's goat?
Also — brass ear-muff lot in the market, waving a work order at our stone. Tamsin nearly launched them into the sea.
Buying? Wonderful. While you choose, did you hear about the miller's goat?
The ear-muff crew packed up after Tamsin's Keynote went to you. The goat's fine, by the way. It ate a kite.
Thirty verses. The whole Kinsong, sung by one troupe. I may cry on my clipboard. I'm allowed.
30 verses sung! That's the whole songbook. Here — gold edging for your Kinsong, and Crown Chimes. You've earned this.
20 verses sung! That's a proper songbook now. Here — you've earned this.
An Etude I copied from an old hymnal — Radiant Mend. Plus Silver Chimes, and your fee. Keep singing.
10 verses sung! That's a proper songbook now. Here — you've earned this.
You're the one from Larkhollow! I'm compiling the Kinsong — every verse in Cantarra. Show me what you've heard and I'll pay in useful things.
Ten verses, twenty, all thirty — every kin you befriend adds a verse. Galewick's wind has lovely acoustics for it.
Odile Graven? There's a verse in the oldest Kinsong about a herd on the Ash Flats. Nobody sings it anymore.
It ends mid-line. Like whoever wrote it couldn't bear to finish.
My study has a cellar behind a curtain of dusk. It won't part for me. A shade voice singing Veil might coax it.
Bring me your Kinsong as it grows. Ten verses, twenty, thirty. I pay in useful things and loud applause.
Parcels in, parcels out. The wind does half my job. The other half is stairs.
A reply from Cindral! 'Doing fine. Fewer burns.' Ha. That's Ash all over.
Here — Silver Chimes and your fee. The Courier Office pays its debts, even the windy ones.
The parcel's for Ash, Hearthkeeper at the foot of Mount Cindral. West over Highscar, then walk till it's hot.
You look like someone who walks a lot. Fancy a courier job? Pays in Chimes.
One parcel for Ash at the Cindral base Hearthrest. Bring me the reply and I'll pay you properly.
Three kites home! The contest's cancelled, but spiritually? Spiritually you won it.
All three! Brackenridge, Highscar and our own cliff vent. You Gusted them free!
The prize Etude — Stormcoil Bolt. Wind and spark together. Loudest thing I own. Take it before I change my mind.
Three kites on three updrafts: the kite ridge on Brackenridge Pass, Highscar's east vent, and our cliff vent past Vane Hall.
Sing Gust at each and the wind lets go. Kites find their own way home. They're smarter than they look.
A gale Keynote! Oh, perfect. The kite contest's ruined — three kites blew off and snagged on updrafts.
A kin singing Gust could shake them loose. Brackenridge ridge, Highscar's east vent, our cliff vent. Please?
Kite contest's on hold. Blame the wind. Actually, don't — it hears.
Work order 212, Galewick Chordstone, routine service. It's all signed, Cantor.
Signed by *whom*? The wind didn't sign it. Get your coils off my stone.
It's a licensed survey guild order. Stamped. Countersigned. There's a wax seal.
Then take your wax seal and sit on it. You there — Tuner with the Keynotes. Find me at Vane Hall. We'll talk.

Signed by *whom*? The wind didn't sign it. Get your coils off my stone.
It's a licensed survey guild order. Stamped. Countersigned. There's a wax seal.
Then take your wax seal and sit on it. You there — Tuner with the Keynotes. Find me at Vane Hall. We'll talk.
Work order 212 is perfectly valid. I'll just… stand here until the Cantor calms down. Could be a while.
Honestly? I joined for the helmet. It's very warm.
Highscar Rise, west. Updraft vents all the way up, and they only lift for a gale voice. Gust, friend.
Gate's shut to the unready. Cantor's orders — Highscar's cliffs eat anyone without Vane Hall's Keynote.
Gloamstair's open. Dress warm — the stair sits in blue hour all day, and the stones up there are silent.
North gate's shut. Gloamstair's gone cold and quiet. Nobody climbs it without the Forge Keynote from Cindral.
My goat ate a kite. Then the string. Then the bit of the contest sign that said 'contest'. She's fine.
The mills turn whether the stones sing or not. But they turn happier when they sing. Don't ask how I know.
Whirlseeds turn the little mills! I named them all. That one's Spin. That one's also Spin.
Lighthouse lamp's been dark since its brass lode went quiet. A spark kin could jolt it awake, I reckon.
Lighthouse is lit again! Ships can see us, gulls can see us. The gulls were a mistake.
You beat Tamsin! She laughed, didn't she? She always laughs. Even when she loses. Especially then.
Vane Hall's all vents and curtains of wind. Don't fight it — argue with it, Tamsin says. I'm still working that out.
